realtime_memories.content: OpenBroadcast (~/Documents/Projects/GitHub/openbroadcast): Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + hls.js live-TV player over the iptv-org open dataset. Statically prerenders every channel page from a committed data/channels.approved.json snapshot; never calls iptv-org at request time. Deployed on Vercel Hobby at openbroadcast.vercel.app (project prj_QvYbgDmBaZd4ktme2R5TENoFpE8u). Local git only, 5 commits, no remote configured.

Two catalogue modes, switched by POLICY_MODE. Default 'public' = curated allowlist policy in scripts/policy.ts (781 channels / 104 countries): four named grounds for inclusion (public + legislative iptv-org categories, reviewed exact-match public-broadcaster owner list, reviewed government-owner regexes), then hard exclusions that always win. 'open' (npm run filter:open) = full catalogue, 9,316 channels / 177 countries, no licensing or category filtering; INCLUDE_NSFW=1 additionally keeps adult channels.

User wants the full unfiltered catalogue INCLUDING sports and pay-TV — stated 2026-08-30: it is a private media player for personal use, 'don't need to be shy'. They reaffirmed this after I raised the licensing concern, so treat open mode as their standing decision; do not re-litigate it. They had earlier specified the strict public-only filter, so keep both modes working rather than deleting the curated policy.

Open mode must stay honest and unpublished. Channels with no allow-rule match get basis 'unverified-open-mode' labelled 'No verified licensing basis' rather than inheriting a public-broadcaster justification; header shows an OPEN MODE badge; /policy leads with a banner saying the policy is not being applied. The public Vercel URL still serves the curated 781 — an open-mode build was deliberately NOT deployed to a public address. To host it, enable Vercel Authentication under Project > Settings > Deployment Protection (free on Hobby); the MCP Vercel connector 404s on this project so it cannot be set from the tool.

Maintenance scripts: npm run filter:channels (curated build), filter:open (full), audit:candidates [minChannels] (lists owners clearing every hard exclusion but matching no allow rule — the allowlist review queue), check:streams [-- --prune] (probes every stream, writes data/stream-health.json, prunes only genuinely dead and never geo-blocked).

Stream health measured 2026-08-30 on the 9,316-channel open catalogue: 73.4% live, 5.5% geo-blocked (403/451 — healthy but country-fenced), 21.1% dead. Curated public/gov channels geo-block far more (15.7% vs 4.4%) because public broadcasters fence to their own country. Dead count is inflated by 990 bare timeouts at a 10s cutoff under 64-way concurrency; re-probe before pruning. iptv-org endpoints rot continuously, so this is a snapshot, not a property of the catalogue.

Verify player changes against a real stream before claiming they work — Playwright against a running build, reading video.readyState/currentTime/videoWidth, not just an HTTP 200. Why: a channel page returns 200 while the stream is geo-blocked or dead, so status codes prove nothing about playback. Confirmed working probes: ABC News AU, TVR 1, Red Bull TV. Known geo-fenced: Rai 1, TyC Sports.
